decided.question: is the calendar's capability gate handed the raw stored role or the normalized one, given `can()` normalizes nothing and a membership can still store the legacy `member`
decided.chose: the normalized role, in both gates — `can(normalizeRole(role), 'view-time-off-calendar')` behind the route and `hasCapability(role, 'ViewTimeOffCalendar')` in the sidebar, so a stored `member` is read as `user`, holds the capability in both spellings, and is answered the page whose row it is drawn
decided.rejected: handing `can()` the raw stored role, which refuses that member the calendar while the sidebar draws its Calendar row
decided.why: rule 2 — the surrounding rule is the one this spec already states two paragraphs above, that capability checks run against `normalizeRole()` and therefore work on today's `admin` / `member` column; the rejected reading is the dead navigation REQ-01-004 forbids, and it is reachable only because this spec is the first to grant a capability to `user`
decided.recordedAt: the **Decided** under `## Roles & Permission Matrix`, which states the choice and both rejected alternatives; carried into the calendar's Guards cell in the contracts Routes table and the paragraph below it, into specs/time-off/README.md's shared-code paragraph, and observed by the new TC-01-UNIT-04, which probes both unions for `member`, `user` and `viewer` and asserts the unnormalized `can('member', …)` is false

decided.question: under the `Month` preset, does back or forward move by the window's own day count or to the adjacent calendar month
decided.chose: the adjacent calendar month — under `Month`, back and forward move to the whole calendar month before or after the displayed one; under `Week` and `2 weeks` they move one preset length, which REQ-01-019 anchors on the caller's `firstDayOfWeek`
decided.rejected: shifting the anchor by the window's day count, which under `Month` produces a 28-to-31-day span across two months
decided.why: rule 2 — REQ-01-019 already carves `Month` out as the first to the last day of the displayed calendar month, and the rejected reading names in the range label a window the preset itself cannot produce
decided.recordedAt: REQ-01-049, whose rule now states all three moves per preset, and its **Decided** naming the rejected reading; observed by TC-01-E2E-03, which now presses `calendar-window-month` and `calendar-prev` and expects one day header per day of the previous calendar month, first to last
